Independent analytical replay of the common-level equations, inverse-slope monotonicity, boundary asymptotics and two-dimensional Schur test
correctness.rationale: The shift in the second coordinate reduces all distinct two-cycles to ordered abscissae u<v with cv=1-aS(u), cu=1-aS(v). Thus the two abscissae are the two inverse points at a common level of g=aS-cx, and the orbit exists exactly when H(k)=k+c(u+v)=1 above the minimum level. Since a>c>0, the vertex is c*epsilon/a strictly in the core; g decreases and increases strictly on the two respective sides. When both inverses are in the core their sum is constant. In the mixed branch the left slope has magnitude at least a-c (the right slope), and with two outer inverses its magnitude is a+c, so H increases throughout. Its lower and two interface values, divided by epsilon, are (a^2+3c^2)/(2a), (a^2-ac+2c^2)/a at the right threshold, and (a^2+c^2)/(a-c) at the left threshold. Inverting these gives the unique branch and all switch values; enforcing the ordered inverses selects the displayed roots. At the first switch the mixed polynomial has derivative -2(a-c) in u, zero epsilon derivative, and second epsilon derivative 2a^2, giving the quadratic onset. The core squared half-gap is 2*epsilon*(1-epsilon/epsilon_*)/a; at the merger the fixed point's one-step polynomial is (lambda+1)(lambda-b). The determinant of the return is b^2 and its trace is 2b+m(u)m(v) for m(x)=aS'(x). This product begins at -a^2, then increases continuously and strictly to c^2 (use the mixed square-root expression and the core 1/epsilon term). Hence the upper Schur condition holds on the whole primitive branch, and the lower condition is R>-(1+b)^2. At equality the other multiplier is -b^2; below it only one has modulus greater than one. Substitution at R=-W yields both formulas for epsilon_s; the separator is R(epsilon_2)=2ac-a^2, including agreement at equality. The double abscissa at epsilon_* is not counted as prime period two.
residual_risks: At neutral multipliers the conclusions are linear, not nonlinear stability claims. For the published range 0<epsilon<1, only its intersection with the proved ranges applies.
